assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action of the processed peptide) underpins a therapeutic class that has changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and is now showing cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery is clear, original and of exceptional lasting impact, with a clean path from physiology to medicine.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the physiology and the biology of GLP-1 action; Mojsov's role in identifying the active truncated peptide is part of the historical record but credit is contested in the literature. Knudsen's contribution is pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues, which I treat as distinct from the core discovery. The three selected names give a coherent physiology-centred configuration.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and very large phase 3 outcome trials. Recognition is timely given clinical uptake over the last several years.
uncertainties: Credit for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) form is disputed and I have not independently verified the priority claims.
Whether the committee wishes to recognize drug development (Knudsen) alongside physiology is unresolved.
Long-term safety of chronic use is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision. The method is original, broadly enabling and has transformed circuit analysis across systems; therapeutic applications (retinal vision restoration) are emerging.
assessment.attribution: Six credited names. The decisive steps appear to be Miesenböck's early genetically encoded light-sensitisation of neurons, the Bamberg/Nagel/Hegemann work on channelrhodopsin, and Boyden/Deisseroth's demonstration of millisecond-scale neuronal control and subsequent tool development. Three-laureate limit forces a difficult choice; my selection spans the early concept, the molecular tool and the neuronal implementation but omits Hegemann, Bamberg and Boyden, which is a real fairness problem.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for roughly two decades; the interpretation is stable. Timely, with possibly shrinking window.
uncertainties: Allocation among six contributors is contentious and may favour a different trio.
Whether a tool/method is judged mainly a discovery in physiology is a committee judgement.
I rely on recollection of the historical record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells that recognise tumour antigen have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. Concept, engineering and clinical proof are all established.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the design of co-stimulated CARs, June the first sustained clinical successes and clinical translation, Rosenberg the early adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified T-cell trials. Other early CAR pioneers (e.g. Eshhar) are not in the supplied credited names, so the available configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of clinical follow-up; benefit in solid tumours is limited and toxicity and manufacturing remain constraints, but the haematological result is firm.
uncertainties: The supplied credit omits some historically important early contributors.
Rosenberg's inclusion depends on whether cell therapy lineage is weighted over CAR design.
Long-term durability and secondary malignancy risk are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and of its role as a nutrient and growth regulator is a conceptual centrepiece of cell growth control, with implications for cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined its function; Schreiber's chemical-biology work on FKBP12-rapamycin set up the target identification. Sabatini's mTORC1 nutrient-sensing work is substantial but I leave it out for a two-person configuration anchored in the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed over three decades; therapeutic use of rapalogs is real but modest relative to the biology.
uncertainties: Whether Schreiber's role is judged decisive versus the Heitman/Hall/Movva yeast-genetics work, which is not fully represented among supplied names.
Sabatini's omission is a judgement; I have not verified any ancillary considerations.
Clinical impact of mTOR inhibitors is narrower than the conceptual impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted to interferon and inflammatory responses, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and neurodegeneration. A clear mechanism with broad conceptual reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP, the decisive step; Barber identified STING. Other credited names (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) were part of the same line of work, with Wu and Sun as trainees in Chen's group, so a two-person prize is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is strongly replicated; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has not yet delivered approved drugs, so impact is still mostly conceptual.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete, which may argue for waiting.
Relative credit between STING discovery by independent groups is something I recall but have not verified.
Role of trainees in the cGAS discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a drug platform. This is a clean path from RNA biology to transformative treatment of a fatal childhood disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and development; the credited pair maps neatly to the discovery and its translation. Other contributors to the SMN2 target biology (e.g. Hua, Singh) are not in the supplied credited list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up; the platform concept has been confirmed across other diseases.
uncertainties: Contributions from other laboratories on the splice target could dilute credit.
The recent RNA-focused Nobel recognition (microRNA, mRNA vaccines) may affect committee appetite.
Long-term outcomes across the full SMA spectrum remain under study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new mode of intracellular signalling from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus and a quality-control logic that matters in diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell physiology. A fundamental discovery of lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and complementarily identified the Ire1-Hac1/Xbp1 axis and its unconventional splicing mechanism, so the pair is well supported by the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is deeply established, with a long record of confirmation; disease-directed drug translation is early.
uncertainties: Medical impact is largely conceptual so far.
Part of a broader proteostasis field that could be recognised in other combinations, which I have not verified.
Possible overlap with prior recognition of related ER and chaperone work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted BCR-ABL inhibition with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the proof of principle for kinase-directed cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound programme, Druker the preclinical rationale and the clinical trials, and Sawyers the resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors; a trio is plausible. Credit of the underlying BCR-ABL oncogene discovery to earlier cytogenetic and molecular work is not in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of follow-up with unambiguous survival benefit; timing is arguably late rather than premature, and prior major prizes have recognised the work.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the underlying discovery of the oncogene as already honoured or separate.
Industry versus academic credit allocation is sensitive.
I recall but have not verified the details of the compound programme history.
